g.text: Connection-setup segment — carries SYN and/or ACK control flags
Segment that also carries application data (piggybacked on the ACK)
Endpoint state after each segment (RFC 9293 §3.3.2 state names)

svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology # TCP three-way handshake + data on the third segment (RFC 9293 §3.5). # Two endpoints, three directed segments carrying the connection-setup # exchange. Each segment's ordinal (1/2/3) is in its edge label. # # HONEST LIMIT (guide/expressing.md known limits — "strict message ordering"): # message ORDER is carried only by the 1/2/3 numbering convention in the # labels, a naming convention that `MEANING-RECOVERY-SOURCE` does not treat as first-class order. # The sequence genre (`FLOWCHART-GENRE-DESIGN`, v0.2) will make order first-class semantics; # until then a reader must trust the ordinal prefixes below. # Likewise, the canonical RFC 9293 figure carries the per-endpoint TCP # STATE (LISTEN, SYN-SENT, …) on the lifelines; the topology genre has no # lifeline-state construct, so the companion `table` block below carries # those states machine-readably — composition (multiple typed blocks in one # document, in document order) is the ruled interim until sequence lands. title "TCP Three-Way Handshake"
# Semantic classes: the label states the MEANING; colour merely renders it, # and the legend derives automatically (spec §2.7). Each segment is classed # by what it does — a reader queries the class, not the arrow colour. class setup "Connection-setup segment — carries SYN and/or ACK control flags" stroke=#2563eb class data "Segment that also carries application data (piggybacked on the ACK)" stroke=#16a34a
node client "Client (active open)" node server "Server (passive open, LISTEN)"
# left-to-right reading: client on the left issues the active open. flow right
# Segment 1: client -> server, SYN, seq=x (flags: SYN) edge client -[1: SYN seq=x]-> server class=setup
# Segment 2: server -> client, SYN+ACK, seq=y ack=x+1 (flags: SYN, ACK) edge server -[2: SYN,ACK seq=y ack=x+1]-> client class=setup
# Segment 3: client -> server, ACK ack=y+1, carrying piggybacked data # (flags: ACK). One segment, so ONE edge; it is both an ACK and a data # carrier, so it is classed as data (the stronger claim). Detail in prose. edge client -[3: ACK ack=y+1 (+ data)]-> server class=data
# Hybrid panels: a second figdown section below (multi-section `MULTI-FIGURE-DOCUMENTS`), # not nested under the scene header. Each section has one genre (`GENRE-KEYWORD-ALLOWLIST`).
# --- panel: separate genre section (main-standard hybrid = multi-section `MULTI-FIGURE-DOCUMENTS`) --- figdown 0.1 table table state "Endpoint state after each segment (RFC 9293 §3.3.2 state names)" | Segment | Client state | Server state | |--------------------|-----------------------|---------------------------| | start | CLOSED | LISTEN | | 1: SYN → | SYN-SENT | SYN-RECEIVED on receipt | | 2: SYN,ACK ← | ESTABLISHED on receipt| SYN-RECEIVED | | 3: ACK → | ESTABLISHED | ESTABLISHED on receipt |
